editorial:
After her father dies in a strange car crash, quiet teen India lives with her unstable mother Evie. Then her mysterious uncle Charlie arrives, charming but creepy, and the house fills with tension. India starts drawn to him even as warning signs pile up. Charlie’s presence changes every dinner, glance, and conversation, making the family home feel dangerous without needing loud shocks. This is a slow, stylish, unsettling thriller that builds dread through small moments rather than big scares.

The acting is strong, especially Mia Wasikowska, Nicole Kidman, and Matthew Goode. India’s quiet nature makes her easy to root for, while Evie’s jealousy adds another layer of conflict. The visuals are sharp and the music feels eerie. The pacing is slow and deliberate, so it may not work for viewers wanting fast action. Pros include strong mood, memorable images, and a bold ending; cons include slow pace and some confusing choices. It is best for fans of psychological thrillers and dark family secrets. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or watch it on 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, India learns Charlie has been killing people around the family, and he tries to pull her into his violent world. She turns on him and shoots him dead. Instead of going to the police, she drives away and embraces the same dark instincts, ending with her aiming a rifle at a sheriff and becoming the new threat.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark family thrillers and slow-building suspense.
